params.body:
## What

`web-browse` had no rhythm, like `instagram-search` until #192. In the day to 2026-09-21 it ran on 70 collect rounds, made 1,308 model calls (more than classify, the largest consumer in the pipeline), took about six minutes of every round, and brought one new signal; about ten in the week. 21 of the 70 rounds were cut off mid-list, and a cut-off round loses the pages it had already read.

## How

- `cadence: {everyHours: 6}`. Nineteen front pages do not change by the quarter hour; four times a day reads each one morning, noon, evening and night. The existing rule holds: it rests only after a round that did its work, and is tried again next round after a failure.
- The collector now tells every adapter when it will be cut off (`ctx.cutOffAt`). `web-browse` starts no new page in the last 80 seconds before that (a page is at most a 15 s fetch and a 60 s model call), keeps what it has, and logs which pages it did not read.
- `rotated()`: the list turns one place per six hours, so the pages at the end today are not at the end every time.
- `test/web-browse-rhythm.test.mjs` pins the rest, the rotation, the early stop and the collector's side of it.

Not in here: the `crawl_cadence` column on the source rows (five say `daily`, fourteen say nothing). Honouring it per source needs a per-source stamp; today the collector stamps all rows of a type at once.

## After the merge

One more `web-browse` round, then the log says `resting until …` for six hours, and a collect round takes about ninety seconds instead of seven minutes.
params.title: web-browse reads its pages four times a day, and keeps what it read
